id_and_class.theory_title: Schwitzgebel's Unreliable Introspection, Indeterminate Boundaries, Metaphysical Humility
id_and_class.summary: Schwitzgebel holds that phenomenal consciousness is real but denies that introspection gives reliable access to it or that it has sharp boundaries. He argues that for some systems, such as a garden snail, it may be neither determinately true nor false that there is something it is like to be them. His ‘crazyism’ adds that every theory of mind and cosmos has bizarre consequences and none compels belief, so his position sets constraints on theories rather than offering one.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Real Experience, Unreliable Introspection, Vague Boundaries

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Schwitzgebel identifies phenomenal consciousness only by example: whatever obvious feature is shared by seeing colours, feeling pain, vivid emotion, imagery, dreaming, and conscious thought, and lacked by hormone regulation, standing knowledge, and unconscious sensory processing.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Left open. Recognizing experience commits one neither to dualism nor to the claim that qualia are scientifically inexplicable, and materialism, dualism, panpsychism, and idealism all yield bizarre consequences when fully developed.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Unspecified; whatever its basis, consciousness is vague, fading through borderline cases instead of switching on at a sharp threshold
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjective experience plainly exists, but our judgments about its character, structure, and even presence are error-prone because attention to experience is unstable.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Schwitzgebel declines to build privacy, infallible acquaintance, intrinsic properties, or nonphysicality into the concept of experience. He defends qualia against strong illusionism while refusing to infer any substantive ontology from them.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Phenomenal experience as a real phenomenon; no commitment about its underlying nature or whether it forms a natural kind.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Introspection is the main source of data but is far less reliable than commonly assumed, which leaves consciousness science with a weak evidence base.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Introspection, Distribution (animals, AI, group entities)
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The borderline consciousness quadrilemma: across the continuum of Earthly systems, either almost nothing is conscious, everything is, a sharp boundary exists somewhere, or consciousness is vague. The first two are implausible, and no naturalistic theory can explain a single synapse flipping experience on, so consciousness is vague.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Uncertain and possibly indeterminate for many systems. Schwitzgebel argues that if materialism is true, the United States is probably conscious, using the case to show how standard criteria generate strange results.
core_claims_and_evidence: Mid-twentieth-century Americans reported dreaming in black and white and later, after colour television, in colour, which suggests that reports track cultural models more than experience.
Careful observers disagree about visual imagery, the richness of peripheral vision, and constant tactile experience of the feet, and no principled method settles these disputes.

Theories such as Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, and higher-order theories specify conditions that come in degrees while treating consciousness as all-or-nothing, so they owe an account of where the cutoff falls.
Every developed metaphysics of mind defies common sense (universal bizarreness) and none compels rational belief (universal dubiety).
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical, drawing on historical and phenomenological evidence about introspective reports

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Historical analysis of dream-colour reports and comparison of visual imagery reports across observers and eras since Galton.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Smithies and Spener argue that the failures Schwitzgebel cites are domain-general, not specific to introspection, and historical variation in reports may reflect changing descriptions, not changing experiences. Critics also charge that borderline consciousness mistakes vagueness in our concept for vagueness in the world, and Kammerer argues materialists can deny group consciousness on principled grounds.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Schwitzgebel offers no mechanism, neural criterion, or positive account of how experience arises, and regards that absence as honest. Whether phenomenal consciousness is a natural kind is left open.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent as a set of epistemic constraints combining realism about experience with agnosticism about its basis; it fits with mainstream naturalism while warning that naturalism itself leads to strange conclusions.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Schwitzgebel holds that current theories give weak grounds for deciding which artificial systems are conscious, and some may be borderline cases with no determinate answer.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since no metaphysics of mind compels belief on this view, the question of survival is left open.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Crazyism holds that something bizarre must be true about mind and cosmos but that we cannot know what.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Without a settled metaphysics of mind, whether a digital copy would be conscious cannot be decided.
